newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht fixed at 67-month-low versus rising dlr.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht fixed at 67-month-low versus rising dlr.

text.p: The Thai baht was on Monday fixed at a new 67-month low against the dollar on Monday as the U.S. unit's gained further steam against other majors, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.71 on Monday, the lowest level since June 1991. The mid-rate was at 25.67 on Friday.
But the baht's fall against the dollar in the interbank spot market was limited by persistent selling of the greenback by some Singaporean players taking profit, dealers said.
At 0259 GMT, the baht was quoted at 25.700/703 to the dollar compared with 25.668-25.671 late on Friday, they added.
"The dollar was still traded relatively low compared with the central bank's fixing. There was continued selling of the dollar from Singapore," said one senior dealer at a local bank.
The dealer said the continued selling of the dollar emerged as players in Singapore believed the dollar's rise against major currencies might have reached its peak.
"The strong demand for baht and rising short-term baht interest rates was also a major factor that prompted some dollar selling against the baht," another dealer at a foreign bank said.
The tighter liquidity pushed the overnight interbank rate up sharply to 11.50-12.00 percent in early trade on Monday from 10.50-10.75 late on Friday, dealers said.

Dealers attributed the tightening liquidity to the fund payment for the Bank of Thailand's bond auction made last Friday and reserving of funds by commercial bank to meet the forthcoming central bank's reserve requirement deadline.
All commercial banks have to meet the central bank's reserve requirement on seventh and 22nd of every month.
"The demand for funds is very strong this morning. The interbank rate will remain high until the passing of the reserve deadline," one dealer at a foreign bank said.
The close of New York market today will also reduce most banks' funding through the swap market, dealers said.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was steady at 9.50/10.00, unchanged from late on Friday, dealers said.
